Scene:
古代的时候，有一个人叫神农。一天，神农正在路上走，一看很多人正在吃一些植物。一些人一吃植物就生病了，神农想帮别人。所以想知道哪些植物能吃，哪些植物不能吃。

The teacher's corrections on this scene:
- 一看很多人正在吃一些植物：看到，一……就
- 神农想帮别人：帮他们，“别(的)” is for “a different type”, and “all else except the spoken one”

The system's item in each run:
Run 1: Incorrect phrase: “神农想帮别人。” Formula: character/name + 想 + 帮助 + specific person/group Correct: “神农想帮助这些人。” “别人” is vague here; “这些人” clearly refers to the people who became sick.
Run 2: Incorrect phrase: “神农想帮别人。所以想知道……” / Formula: Subject + 想 + verb; therefore + subject + 想知道… / Correct: “神农想帮助人们，所以想知道哪些植物能吃，哪些植物不能吃。” The second sentence has no subject, which makes the reference slightly unclear. Adding “神农” makes the meaning complete.
Run 3: Incorrect phrase: “神农想帮别人。所以想知道……” / Formula: Subject + 想 + verb, 所以 + verb phrase / Correct: “神农想帮助人们，所以想知道哪些植物能吃，哪些植物不能吃。” “所以想知道” needs to be connected to the previous clause rather than standing as a separate sentence.

You compare feedback items that the same automatic system gave, in separate runs, about the same place in one scene a learner of Chinese wrote. You get the scene, the teacher's corrections on it (reference), and one item per run (some runs may have flagged nothing there).

Return:
- same_error: true if every run's item points at the same error (or the same set of errors) in the learner's words.
- equivalent_fix: true if every run's corrected text is correct and fixes that error in a way the teacher would accept as the same fix -- different wording counts as equivalent when each is a correct fix of the same problem (she often accepts alternatives, e.g. 怕/担心). false if any run fixes a different error, leaves the error, or introduces a new one.
- reason: one short sentence.
